announcements.text: Welcome to AP Computer Science A! Please review the syllabus linked in Materials and complete the intro survey by Friday.
Reminder: Unit 2 test on Friday. Review String methods and Scanner input. Office hours Tuesday and Thursday after school.
AP Exam registration deadline is next Monday March 3. Sign up in the counseling office if you haven't already.
No class Thursday due to PSAT testing day. Use the time to work on your BankAccount project.
Welcome to Web Dev! Make sure you have VS Code installed and a GitHub account created before next class.
Great work on the portfolio projects everyone! I've posted some exemplary examples in Materials for inspiration.
Reminder: Weather API project due Wednesday. Make sure your API key is working. See me if you need help with fetch.
Welcome to AP CSP! This course is about big ideas in CS not just coding. Come ready to think critically and creatively.
Innovation presentations start next week. Sign up for your presentation slot on the shared Google Doc.
AP CSP exam is May 12. Create Task portfolio due to College Board by April 30. No extensions possible.

Annual USCG near-coastal safety inspection scheduled for May 7. Lucky Strike will be at Marina Slip B-14 starting 0800. Pre-position every equipment item for visual inspection and have expiry tags facing out so they can be photographed in place.

Pre-inspection prep checklist posted in Materials. Verify every expiry tag photograph each mounting point and stage handheld items on the salon table. Marisol will run the dry-bag and PFD count from the forward cabin locker.

Inspection complete. Result 13 PASS / 5 FAIL out of 18 total items. CRITICAL findings — EQ-008 Visual Distress Flare Kit expired Dec 2025 / EQ-004 Type IV throwable flotation missing from stern locker. Additional FAILs — EQ-002 cabin extinguisher gauge in red / EQ-014 EPIRB battery expired Mar 2026 / EQ-017 bilge pump float switch broken. Low-confidence items needing daylight re-shoot — EQ-011 bow nav light housing chip / EQ-018 MARPOL placard fade.

Prioritized repair and replacement list with rough costs. P0 immediate — EQ-008 flare kit $75 / EQ-004 throwable Type IV $35 / EQ-014 EPIRB battery service $185. P1 this week — EQ-002 cabin extinguisher $40 / EQ-017 bilge pump $115. P2 deferred — re-shoot low-confidence items EQ-011 and EQ-018 in daylight. Estimated total replacement budget approximately $450. Vendor contacts in mat_010.
Prior-year USCG near-coastal safety inspection scheduled for May 9. Lucky Strike will be at Marina Slip B-14 starting 0800. All equipment must be staged for visual inspection.

Prior-year inspection complete. Result all 18 items PASS. Warning flags for next year — EQ-008 flare kit expires Dec 2025 / EQ-014 EPIRB battery rated to Mar 2026 / EQ-002 cabin extinguisher gauge trending downward. Schedule replacements before May 2026 inspection.

coursework.description: Write a Java program that demonstrates the use of int double boolean and String variables. Include type casting examples.

coursework.description: What method of the Scanner class is used to read an integer from the user?
coursework.title: Scanner Input Quiz

coursework.description: Write a GradeCalculator program that takes a numeric score and outputs the letter grade using if-else chains.

coursework.description: Create programs that use while loops to generate number patterns: pyramid triangle and diamond shapes in the console.
coursework.title: While Loop Patterns

coursework.description: Implement methods that use for loops to find min max sum and average of integer arrays.

coursework.description: Design and implement a BankAccount class with instance variables constructor deposit withdraw and getBalance methods.

coursework.description: Implement a StudentRoster program using ArrayList with add remove search and sort operations.

coursework.description: Complete Free Response Questions 1-3 from the 2023 AP CS A exam practice set. Show all work.

coursework.description: Create a personal portfolio webpage using semantic HTML5 elements. Must include header nav main and footer sections.

coursework.description: Style the provided HTML document using only CSS selectors. Demonstrate class id descendant and pseudo-class selectors.
coursework.title: CSS Selectors Challenge

coursework.description: Build a responsive card layout using CSS Flexbox. Cards should wrap and maintain consistent spacing on all screen sizes.
coursework.title: Flexbox Layout Project

coursework.description: Build a functional calculator using HTML CSS and JavaScript. Must handle addition subtraction multiplication and division.
coursework.title: JavaScript Calculator

coursework.description: Create an interactive todo list application using DOM manipulation. Features: add delete and mark complete.
coursework.title: DOM Todo List App

coursework.description: Build a weather dashboard that fetches data from a public API and displays current conditions and forecast.

coursework.description: Revise and expand your personal portfolio with JavaScript interactivity and responsive design. Deploy to GitHub Pages.
coursework.title: Final Portfolio Revision

coursework.description: Convert between binary decimal and hexadecimal. Complete all 20 conversion problems showing your work.
coursework.title: Number Systems Worksheet

coursework.description: Explain the difference between TCP and UDP. Give one example use case for each.
coursework.title: Internet Protocols Quiz

coursework.description: Design flowcharts for three algorithms: linear search binary search and bubble sort. Use proper flowchart symbols.
coursework.title: Algorithm Flowcharts

coursework.description: Write a 2-page research paper on data privacy concerns with social media platforms. Cite at least 3 sources.
coursework.title: Data Privacy Research Paper

coursework.description: Create a 5-minute presentation on a computing innovation and its societal impact. Include benefits and risks.
coursework.title: Innovation Impact Presentation
